name: Free Body Fluid Load Transfer Mechanisms
goal: How two-way coupling between fluid and a FREE, unconstrained rigid body is implemented in MPM, with emphasis on the algorithmic mechanism converting fluid effects into net rigid-body force and torque. Prioritize bodies that translate, rotate, slide and are swept by the flow. In particular, identify literature explaining why simply assigning a mass-weighted or averaged grid velocity to a rigid body each substep, WITHOUT a separately accumulated force or impulse, fails to produce a physically meaningful free-body response, and contrast that failure with correct formulations in the same coupling family.
summary: FREE-BODY COUPLING IS PHYSICALLY MEANINGFUL ONLY when fluid loading is represented as a generalized force/impulse (three force plus three torque) or an equal-and-opposite constraint reaction, then integrated through Newton-Euler dynamics; VELOCITY OVERWRITING ALONE IS NOT COUPLING [Aly14, Akb18b, Hyd19]. Route 1, pressure/stress loading: solve pressure by projection/PPE, evaluate traction t = sigma.n at surface particles, level-set/SDF quadrature points or stress points, and accumulate F = sum(w_q t_q), tau = sum(w_q (x_q - x_c) x t_q), then update translation and rotation from these resultants [Aly14, Fal18, Xu09, Zha17c]. Moving-control-volume alternatives avoid noisy surface derivatives by obtaining the same force/torque from momentum balance [Nan17, Xia99]. Route 2, grid/constraint exchange: accumulate the reaction or impulse at grid nodes/markers and apply its negative to the fluid, torque taken about the body centre at each reaction location [Kim16b, Bha19, Aan18, Tak20]. APIC/MPM transfers give a conservative particle-grid basis [Jia16]; CPIC and interface-quadrature MPM supply moving-boundary compatibility [Hu18, Fan20]. WHAT FAILS: assigning a mass-weighted grid velocity merely imposes KINEMATICS. It supplies neither a separately accumulated impulse nor a torque, so body momentum is REPLACED rather than TRANSFERRED, and rotation becomes sampling-dependent. The literature explicitly rejects velocity equilibration for unresolved bodies, requiring a drag/load model instead [Hyd19]; conservative impulse coupling is the corrective formulation [Akb18b]. TOP-RANKED: Hu18, Aly14, Gis19b.
